why: Every primary needs a backup at least as large, so after sorting descending the best pairing is adjacent: (1st, 2nd), (3rd, 4th), ... with the smaller of each pair as primary. The answer is the sum of the elements at odd positions of the descending order.
hints: The largest server can never be a primary that earns its full value unless something at least as large backs it. Who should back whom?
Sort descending. Pair the 1st with the 2nd, the 3rd with the 4th, and so on; the 2nd, 4th, 6th... are primaries. An exchange argument shows no other pairing gives a bigger primary sum.
Sort once and sum every second element starting at index 1. O(n log n) time; with an odd n the smallest server is left unused.
pitfalls: Use 64-bit-safe sums (Python is fine): the total can exceed 2^31.
With an odd number of servers, the smallest one is left out, not the largest.
Equal capacities are allowed as primary and backup (>= not >).
constraints:
• 1 <= n <= 2 * 10^5
  • 1 <= memory[i] <= 10^9
  • Not stated in the source; reasonable bounds.
